# authwise_guard_trusted_issuer_rules (Data Source)

A rule of a Guard trusted issuer: a machine holding a token the issuer signed for `subject` may join the network with it. `subject` is the token's `sub` claim, matched exactly: there are no patterns, so no neighbouring subject joins on it. One rule per subject in an issuer. The node is named `<node_name_prefix>-<display name>`, the display name the machine sends when it joins; with `node_name_prefix` unset, the issuer's `display_name` as a DNS label is the prefix, so a name repeated across issuers says which issuer joined it. It is added to `node_group`, and counts against `max_nodes` (1 to 1000; unset is 100). `ephemeral` removes a node once it has been offline an hour, or as soon as it leaves the network. Changes apply to joins from now on; joined nodes keep what they joined with. Changing `subject` replaces the rule. Deleting a rule stops further joins; joined nodes stay. This data source lists every one under a parent.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `tenant_id` (String) The kit tenant's id (`t-…`) the Guard row belongs to. Guard has no tenant of its own since the tenant collapse (tf#65). The provider's `tenant_id` is not used.

### Optional

- `network_id` (String) Parent identifier `network_id`; overrides the provider default.
- `trusted_issuer_id` (String) Parent identifier `trusted_issuer_id`; overrides the provider default.

### Read-Only

- `guard_trusted_issuer_rules` (Attributes List) Every trusted_issuer_rule under the parent, in the order the API lists them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--guard_trusted_issuer_rules))

- `max_nodes` (Number)

- `node_count` (Number)
